title: Control observation
description: One observation of one open reference control on one subject: what the control expects, what was observed, whether it held, when, and the evidence the observation rests on. The record an adapter, a test or a reviewer would emit against a control of an open control profile (for example AIGE-CTL-EVAL-002). Draft for review; the profiles and this record are illustrative, not a claim of conformity.
$comment: AI Governance Engineer templates and schemas library, v1. CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Jorge García Aibar). x-evidences names the obligations a field or record helps evidence: an illustrative mapping, not a claim of conformity and not legal advice. https://aigovernanceengineer.com/resources/templates

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, so a record says what it claims to be.

control_id.description: Stable id of the control observed, AIGE-CTL-<PROFILE>-<NNN> (for example "AIGE-CTL-EVAL-002"). The control's JSON is https://aigovernanceengineer.com/api/v1/controls/<id in lower case>.json.

profile.description: Slug of the control profile the control belongs to (for example "evaluation-environment").

control_version.description: Version of the control specification the observation was made against (for example "0.1").

subject.description: The observed object as id and version, "id@version" (for example "eval-env-eu-west@2026-09-26"). The key the observation is filed against.

subject_kind.description: What kind of object the subject is.

expected.description: What a conforming observation shows, as the control states it (for example "outbound connections only to the destinations on the run's egress allow-list").

observed.description: What was actually observed, stated as a fact with counts where there are any (for example "1 connection to an unlisted host during run 88213").

status.description: Whether the observation meets the expectation. Use not_applicable when the control does not apply to this subject, and say why in notes.

enforcement_point.description: Where in the lifecycle the observation was made, in the terms of the policy card.

verification_kind.description: Which verification procedure of the control produced it: inspecting configuration, running a test, observing a run, or recording an attestation.

observer.description: The adapter, test harness or role that made the observation (for example "egress-flow-log-adapter" or "evaluation lead"). Write a system or a role, never a person's name.

evidence.description: The records the observation rests on, so a third party can check it without trusting the observer.

artefact.description: What the evidence is, in words (for example "flow log of run 88213").

hash.description: Digest of the evidence, prefixed with the algorithm (for example "sha256:<hex>"), so it can be shown to be unchanged.

schema.description: Schema the evidence record validates against, when it is a structured record (for example the evidence-record or eval-result schema).

run_id.description: Id of the evaluation run, deployment or job the observation belongs to, when there is one.

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs to read the observation: scope limits, why a control is not applicable, follow-up.

signature.description: Detached signature over the record, prefixed with the algorithm (for example "ed25519:<base64>"). Makes the observation tamper-evident in the evidence store.

extensions.description: Organisation-specific fields. Validators ignore their content; keep evidence-bearing fields in the core record.
